content: Co-dydramol is a generic name that refers to a combination of dihydrocodeine tartrate and paracetamol. It is primarily used to alleviate moderate pain. Co-dydramol belongs to a group of combination medications available in the UK and other countries. Other examples of such combination drugs include Co-codaprin (a mixture of aspirin and codeine), Co-codamol (a combination of dihydrocodeine and paracetamol), and Co-proxamol (a combination of dextropropoxyphene and paracetamol). Each Co-dydramol tablet contains 500 mg of paracetamol. When the dihydrocodeine content is less than 7.5 mg per tablet, the medication can be sold over the counter at pharmacies without a prescription. However, formulations with higher dihydrocodeine concentrations are classified as prescription-only medications. There are four available strengths of dihydrocodeine tartrate in Co-dydramol tablets: 1. 7.46 mg of dihydrocodeine: This formulation is marketed under the brand name Paramol. 2. 10 mg of dihydrocodeine: This is referred to as Co-dydramol 10/500 in the British Approved Name (BAN) system. If a prescription does not specify the strength, this is the default preparation that should be dispensed. 3. 20 mg of dihydrocodeine: Known as Co-dydramol 20/500 in the BAN system, this formulation is sold under the brand name Remedeine. 4. 30 mg of dihydrocodeine: This is labeled as Co-dydramol 30/500 in the BAN system and is marketed as Remedeine Forte. The naming convention for Co-dydramol and similar drugs follows a specific pattern, where the prefix cosignifies combination. This naming system is widely used in the British National Formulary (BNF) for various combination medications. Examples include antibiotics, gastrointestinal treatments, antihypertensive agents, diuretics, anti-Parkinsonian drugs, and others. Additionally, this naming convention is applied to medications for migraine management, such as Co-dergocrine and Co-careldopa. Another notable example of an opioid combination drug is Co-phenotrope, also known as Lomotil. Unlike Co-dydramol, Co-phenotrope is a non-analgesic combination of diphenoxylate and atropine, primarily used as an anti-diarrheal agent.
